articles.title: VRT MAX arrives in Music Assistant
articles.dek: A first contribution brings Flemish public radio, podcasts, favourites and listening progress into Music Assistant.
body: Music Assistant can now connect directly to VRT MAX, the streaming service of the Flemish public broadcaster. Bram Goolaerts’ new provider covers live stations including Radio 1, Radio 2, Studio Brussel, MNM and Klara, alongside listen-back programmes, podcasts and search. Live radio works without signing in.

Connecting an account adds on-demand playback, Mijn lijst library syncing and resume positions that carry across devices. The provider supports multiple instances, so people in one household can keep separate accounts, and listen-back episodes can expose played songs as chapters in Now Playing.
This is Goolaerts’ first merged contribution to the Music Assistant server. Welcome, Bram—and congratulations on landing an unusually complete first PR.

articles.title: The iOS energy widget makes room for gas and batteries
articles.dek: Home Assistant’s glanceable energy view now carries four parts of a household’s energy picture, including two-way battery flow.
body: Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves expanded the Home Assistant iOS energy widget beyond grid and solar. Battery discharge is stacked above the chart axis, charging below it, while gas appears as a separate figure because its statistics may be measured in volume rather than energy.

The calculation ports the frontend’s consumption split so energy used to charge a battery is not counted as household demand. Cost combines electricity and gas, and adaptive layouts keep all four sources usable on the small widget and Lock Screen accessories.
The work continues Gonçalves’s August run on the widget, after Lock Screen sizing, a reload action for missing data and clearer period and refresh-time information landed earlier in the month.
articles.continuity: Part of a month-long series improving Home Assistant’s energy widgets across iPhone and Lock Screen layouts.

articles.title: ESPHome’s serial setup learns there is more than Wi‑Fi
articles.dek: Improv Serial can now describe Ethernet, Thread and modem connectivity, opening setup and discovery to devices without a Wi‑Fi radio.
body: ESPHome’s Improv Serial component now understands the wider network stack instead of depending entirely on Wi‑Fi. Keith Burzinski’s change lets the component build and run on devices with Wi‑Fi disabled or absent—including Ethernet-only boards—and adds the Improv protocol’s new Get Network State command.

Compatible clients can ask whether a device is online, see which interfaces it has—Wi‑Fi, Ethernet, Thread or modem—and receive web-server URLs for connected interfaces. The provisioning path also stops reporting stale success while a device is still leaving its previous Wi‑Fi network.
It continues a broader multi-interface theme in Burzinski’s recent ESPHome work, following August changes to default-route arbitration across Ethernet and Wi‑Fi.
articles.continuity: Builds on August work making ESPHome’s network stack more deliberate about multiple active interfaces.

articles.title: Removed Bluetooth adapters no longer leave ghost connections
articles.dek: Home Assistant’s Bluetooth layer now disconnects clients tied to an unregistered scanner, keeping real links and slot accounting in sync.
body: Radek Podgorny traced a stubborn Bluetooth state mismatch to scanner removal. Home Assistant cleared its bookkeeping when an adapter disappeared, but connections made through that adapter could remain alive, continuing to deliver notifications while occupying a slot the system believed was free.

The Bluetooth manager now tracks clients per scanner and disconnects them during unregister, while avoiding clients that have already moved to another route. The change covers local adapters and ESPHome proxies, with weak references and bounded cleanup so a dropped client cannot leak or stall shutdown.

Podgorny verified the local path on real BlueZ hardware: disabling the adapter dropped the kernel link, and enabling it again allowed a clean reconnect. The remote-proxy path has automated coverage but was not part of that hardware test.

articles.title: Music Assistant sharpens the first response to bug reports
articles.dek: Six connected changes make duplicate detection broader and more precise, preserve the full triage record and put a plain-language gist atop long reports.
body: A six-PR sequence from Chris overhauled how Music Assistant’s support repository digests incoming reports. The index now strips repeated issue-form boilerplate from ranking, includes all existing issues instead of only the newest 2,500, and shows up to five related posts behind stricter confidence thresholds.

The same series refuses to append to an index built with an incompatible schema, model or vector width, and stores the full triage decision rather than only retrieval scores. Maintainers can now inspect missing fields, labels, pings and deterministic findings when judging whether the automation helped.
Reports longer than 1,500 characters also receive a three-line gist covering what the reporter was doing, what happened and what they expected—without nagging people who already supplied detail.

articles.title: Konyks sockets gain an always-on indicator setting
articles.dek: Two device quirks and a matching Home Assistant translation expose a light mode the sockets support but their Tuya cloud schemas omit.
body: New contributor minimicro34 added quirks for the Konyks Priska Max 3 FR and Priska Duo FR. Both devices were observed supporting four indicator modes—including always on—even though their cloud schemas list only relay, position and off; fixtures and regression coverage preserve the missing value.

A companion Home Assistant change supplies the readable translation for Tuya’s light-mode selector. Together, the three PRs carry the capability from device knowledge in the shared library through to a label users can understand in Home Assistant.
These are minimicro34’s first merged contributions to both tuya-device-handlers and Home Assistant Core. Welcome to both projects.
